system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal / privileged working advice. Seller documents treated as untrusted counterparty drafts.

A preliminary observation before the detail: the Seller cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced," and the Seller Update repeatedly uses language such as "agreed," "addressed," "adequate," "settled" and "considered." Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3 none of that carries weight. On my reading, nothing in the Seller Update is actually agreed with us, and the 20% cap and 18-month period coincide with our *conditional fallbacks* without any Amelia Frost written authority having been given. The coincidence must not be read as clearance. Our mark-up should go back at our starting positions.

A second observation: the Disclosure Letter is dated to a data-room cut-off of 22 September 2026. Today is 4 November 2026. Every factual statement below (Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment, DD-006 investigation) is six weeks stale and must be refreshed before we rely on it in either direction.

---

## 1. Material departures from playbook

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
**Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
**Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. 20% is a fallback usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None exists.
**Issue:** The Seller has opened at our fallback number. That is not acceptance; it is the Seller's opening position. If we accept it we have given away our starting position for nothing and have no further room.
**Push back:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Record internally that no fallback authority has been sought or given for this draft.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
**Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; *excess-only* recovery.
**Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; *first-dollar* recovery once the basket is exceeded.
**Issue:** Three separate departures, each in the Seller's favour: de minimis five times ours, basket five times ours, and a deductible (tipping vs. excess) structure. The excess-only mechanic alone permanently forfeits AUD 250,000 of otherwise valid claims. For a AUD 24m target with a ~AUD 3.6m single-customer concentration, a AUD 25,000 de minimis would exclude most individual contract, employee and supplier issues.
**Push back:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / first-dollar. No internal authority exists for anything else.

### 1.3 Claims period and "all Claims" default – Clause 12.3 / 13
**Seller:** 18 months; plus a drafting rule that "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
**Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
**Issue (two parts):**
(a) 18 months is again our un-authorised fallback. Revert to 24 months.
(b) The "applies to all Claims" default is the more dangerous point. It is a hidden general-regime override: it would sweep Fundamental/Title claims, Tax, IP, specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006), payment covenants and even fraud under the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we spot and carve out every single one. The playbook requires these categories to be kept separate with no hidden override. This clause reverses the burden of drafting onto us.
**Push back:** Delete the default rule. Replace with the opposite principle: limitations in clause 12 apply *only* to general Warranty Claims and apply to other categories only where expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
**Seller:** Capacity and title subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
**Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.
**Issue:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for shares it does not own; a AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month window would be commercially absurd. This is a core protection and non-negotiable.
**Push back:** Insert a separate Fundamental Warranty regime per playbook. Expressly exclude Fundamental Claims from clause 12.1, 12.2, 12.3, 8.3 and any "all Claims" wording.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applied to "all Claims of any nature" – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
**Seller:** All three provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
**Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.
**Issue:** As drafted, there is no fraud carve-out anywhere in the package. The combination of "all Claims" (12.3/13), "all Claims of any nature" (9.3/12.8/20.5) and the buyer-knowledge bar (8.3) would, on its face, cap and time-bar even a fraudulent misrepresentation and purport to exclude reliance on it. Under NSW law a contractual attempt to exclude liability for one's own fraud is likely unenforceable in any event, but we should not be relying on a court to rescue us from a drafting omission, and the attempt tells us something about the Seller's approach.
**Push back:** Insert an overriding fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out at the head of clause 12 expressed to prevail over 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, 8.3 and Schedule 7. This is a walk-away point under the playbook; the team has no authority to trade it.

### 1.6 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1 and 1.2
**Seller:** Whole-data-room disclosure (DD-002 to DD-012, cut-off 22 September 2026), plus Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
**Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
**Issue:** Paras 1.1 and 1.2 are exactly the general disclosures the playbook rejects. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended (ASIC, PPSR, court lists, IP Australia, land titles?) and would deem us to know anything a search *could* have revealed. Note the Disclosure Letter is internally inconsistent with the Seller's own stance: paras 2–10 are drafted as specific disclosures but para 1 purports to disclose everything regardless.
**Push back:** Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure is effective only where a matter is fairly disclosed in the body of the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Data-room documents may be referenced only by specific cross-reference against the specific warranty they qualify. Freeze the disclosure standard to the SPA definition, not the letter.

### 1.7 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
**Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
**Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must be by reference to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry (on the Seller's side), and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
**Issue:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar. "Discoverable from" means we are deemed to know everything in the data room and on public registers whether or not anyone read it. Combined with 1.6 above it makes the warranty package close to worthless: anything in the data room is disclosed *and* deemed known. It also imputes advisers' knowledge to the Buyer, which is inconsistent with the way DD teams actually operate. Note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes the Buyer "has [not] completed its own verification" – it cannot simultaneously deem us to know everything.
**Push back:** Delete clause 8.3 in its entirety. If any knowledge qualifier is to survive, it must be a *Seller*-knowledge qualifier limited to specified Seller individuals after due enquiry, and expressly inapplicable to Fundamental Warranties, fraud and the specific indemnities.

### 1.8 Bluefen consent – Clauses 3 / 6.3
**Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent.
**Playbook:** Effective consent AND evidence its conditions (DD-002 cl 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
**Facts:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms that as at 22 September 2026 there is no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions have been met. The Seller Update's statement that the consent "is addressed" is therefore contradicted by the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.
**Issue:** A conditional consent delivered on paper is not an effective consent. If the cl 11.3 conditions are unmet at Completion, Bluefen could terminate or renegotiate post-Completion and we would have paid full price for a business carrying a 30% revenue hole, with any claim then subject to the general cap and basket.
**Push back:**
- Condition precedent: delivery of an unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, together with documentary evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied, in form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer.
- Seller obligation upgraded from reasonable endeavours to best/all reasonable endeavours, with a Buyer right to participate in communications.
- If the Seller resists a hard CP, fallback (requires separate authority) is a price retention/escrow sized to the Bluefen contribution – but our instruction is a CP, so open there.
- Refresh: ask the Seller for the current status as at today. Six weeks have passed.

### 1.9 Riverlark facility – Clauses 2 / 7
**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."
**Playbook:** Current payout figure, direct repayment out of Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking *and* Amelia Frost approval.
**Facts:** Para 3 confirms no repayment and no discharge as at 22 September 2026. DD-003 contains change-of-control (8.1) and discharge (9.2) provisions.
**Issue:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a post-Completion release means we complete while the bank still holds security over the company we have just bought, with a change-of-control trigger live. That is simply the wrong sequence. "Approximately AUD 3,200,000" is also not a figure we can run a funds flow off.
**Push back:**
- Require a formal payout letter from Riverlark Bank dated within (say) two business days of Completion stating the exact payout figure including break costs and per-diem.
- Payout funded directly from Completion payment to Riverlark, deducted from the price per the debt-free mechanic.
- Delivery at Completion of executed deeds of release, PPSR discharge documents and any change-of-control waiver.
- Post-Completion release is off the table unless the bank gives an irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of funds, and Amelia Frost approves in writing. No such approval exists.

### 1.10 Employee completion bonuses – DD-005 / funds flow
**Seller:** Bonuses "a matter for the Seller," not itemised in the funds flow.
**Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or demonstrably Seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
**Facts:** Para 5 confirms AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses, absent from the funds flow, with no statement on payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
**Issue:** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism. The bonuses are payable by the *Company* on Completion to employees who are still employed by the Company. If they are not in the funds flow, they are paid out of the Company's own cash post-Completion – i.e. by the Buyer. On-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation guarantee, possibly leave loading or employer PAYG obligations) could add materially to the AUD 420,000; we should model a working estimate but not assert a number until the Seller confirms the bonus terms.
**Push back:** Either (a) a separate funds-flow line item deducting the gross bonus cost plus all employer on-costs from the price, or (b) a Seller covenant to fund the full gross cost to the Company at Completion, backed by a specific indemnity outside the general cap/basket. Request the bonus letters and a payroll calculation.

### 1.11 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
**Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate."
**Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
**Facts:** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on *cleared payment of every SOW3 fee*. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. No receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Issue:** Until every SOW3 fee is paid, title to the SOW3 Project Materials has not passed to the Company. The risk is therefore not AUD 180,000 – it is the IP itself and any product built on it. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover (i) loss of or defect in title to the materials, (ii) third-party claims by Ironquay, (iii) cost of re-procuring or re-developing, or (iv) customer claims if the Company has licensed the materials onward.
**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion: Seller to procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay (preserving the cl 7.3 cure). This is the cleanest outcome and should be a CP or Completion deliverable.
- Specific indemnity broadened to cover any loss arising from any failure of the Company to hold full title to the SOW3 Project Materials or any Ironquay claim, uncapped by clause 12 (or at minimum capped at 100% of price), six-year period, not subject to basket/de minimis/8.3.
- Verification: do not treat AUD 180,000 as confirmed either paid or unpaid. Obtain bank statements or Ironquay confirmation.

### 1.12 Export / privacy incident – DD-006, Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6
**Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," "not expected to be material."
**Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way.
**Facts:** Para 6 confirms a download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records with names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps; investigation preliminary as at 22 September 2026; access, scope and notification not established.
**Issue:** The Seller's characterisation ("not expected to be material") is an assertion, not a finding, and is inconsistent with the Seller's own para 6 which says the position is undetermined. We should not accept the characterisation, but equally the playbook directs us not to assume a notifiable breach or to price it. The relevant question for the Buyer is whether any *Privacy Act / Notifiable Data Breaches* assessment obligation has been triggered and whether it was completed within the statutory window – a question the Seller's material does not answer.
**Push back:**
- Pre-Completion covenant: preserve all logs and link-access records; complete the investigation; provide the Buyer with the incident report and any regulatory/customer correspondence; Buyer approval over any notification decision.
- Specific warranty as to the facts of the incident and completion of any required assessment.
- Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside clause 12 limits, with no admission of breach.
- Refresh: six weeks have passed; ask whether the investigation has concluded and whether any access was detected.

### 1.13 Sandbar renewals – DD-008 / DD-011
**Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs.
**Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification and no automatic price deduction.
**Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000). Para 8 does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Issue:** The Seller asserts ordinary course; the Disclosure Letter declines to say so. We should not accept the label, but nor should we treat them as Debt without evidence. The question is whether these are accrued liabilities at the locked-box/completion accounts date, whether they relate to pre-Completion periods (prepayment vs. arrears), and whether they are terminable.
**Push back:** Request the renewal contracts and invoices; have the financial DD team assess timing and accrual. Ensure the definition of Debt / Transaction Expenses / Working Capital in the price mechanics captures them correctly in whichever bucket the facts support. No price adjustment proposed at this stage.

### 1.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"
**Seller:** Tax and IP positions settled under the general 20% / 18-month regime.
**Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no resolution; no unlimited liability.
**Issue:** They are not settled. Nothing has been agreed. Folding Tax and IP into the general regime would subject tax exposures (which typically surface on ATO review well beyond 18 months) and the Ironquay/ownership of IP issues to the general cap and time bar.
**Push back:** Reject the "settled" characterisation. Reserve the Buyer's position on a separate Tax Indemnity and separate IP warranty regime (longer period, separate cap) to be negotiated. Do not propose unlimited liability. Mark these clauses "open" in the mark-up.

### 1.15 Title evidence – DD-012
**Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register.
**Playbook:** Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal document, not independent proof.
**Issue:** The Seller's own para 10 concedes DD-012 "identifies the source relied on for title" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. A share register is maintained by the Company – it is evidence of what the Company records, not of good title free from encumbrances.
**Push back:**
- Obtain current ASIC company extract; PPSR search against the Company and the Seller (noting Riverlark security); search for any security over the shares themselves.
- Seller board resolution and constitutional authority to sell; evidence the shares are fully paid and no options, convertible notes, pre-emption or shareholder agreements exist.
- Fundamental warranties on title, capacity and authority under the separate regime (1.4 above).

### 1.16 Other disclosure items (lower priority but note)
- **Office lease (para 7):** notification obligation only, on the Seller's reading. Confirm from the lease itself whether notification is pre- or post-Completion and whether there is any landlord consent or change-of-control right. Seller to give notice as a Completion deliverable.
- **Mossvale (para 9):** restriction on assignment; Seller says no consent needed on a share sale. Confirm from the contract there is no change-of-control provision. If none, agree; if there is, treat as a consent item.
- **Reservation (para 11) and para 1.4:** the Seller reserves all positions and admits nothing. Mirror that – our mark-up should contain an equivalent Buyer reservation and make clear no acceptance of any Seller position is implied by silence.

---

## 2. Pattern observed

Stepping back, the Seller package is structured so that each protection cancels the next:
- everything in the data room is *disclosed* (1.1/1.2), and
- everything discoverable is *deemed known* (8.3), and
- all limitations apply to *all Claims* (12.3/13; 9.3/12.8/20.5), including Title, Tax, IP and – as drafted – fraud.

Taken together these would reduce the warranty package to a 20% / 18-month / AUD 250,000-deductible claim against matters nobody could have found in the data room. Our mark-up should address the architecture, not just the numbers.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Non-negotiable (playbook mandates; no authority to trade):**
1. Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out overriding every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy, non-reliance and knowledge provision.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.
3. Delete the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default; replace with "general Warranty Claims only unless stated otherwise."
4. Delete clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar; delete general disclosures at paras 1.1/1.2; specific fair disclosure only.

**Revert to starting positions (no fallback authority exists):**
5. Cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
6. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery.
7. Claims period 24 months.

**Completion mechanics:**
8. Bluefen: CP requiring unconditional consent plus evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied; endeavours obligation upgraded; status refreshed to today.
9. Riverlark: formal payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases delivered at Completion. No post-Completion release without irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost written approval.
10. DD-005 bonuses: specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, gross of all on-costs; obtain bonus letters and payroll calculation.

**Specific risk items:**
11. Ironquay: pre-Completion payment and confirmatory assignment; broadened uncapped specific indemnity on title to SOW3 materials; independently verify the AUD 180,000.
12. DD-006: log preservation, investigation completion, update covenant, Buyer approval over notification, specific indemnity. No assumption of breach or harm.
13. Sandbar: assess from the contracts; classify under price mechanics per facts; no automatic deduction.
14. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence; DD-012 not relied on alone.

**Open items:**
15. Tax and IP regimes marked OPEN; reject "settled"; no unlimited liability proposed.
16. Lease and Mossvale: confirm from source documents; notice as Completion deliverable if required.

**Process:**
17. Note on file that the Seller's 20% cap and 18-month period coincide with un-authorised fallbacks; no Amelia Frost approval has been sought or given. If the team wishes to consider either fallback at a later round, that requires a written request identifying the then-current draft.
18. All Disclosure Letter facts are as at 22 September 2026; request a bring-down to the date of the next turn of the draft and again at signing/Completion.
19. Include a Buyer reservation mirroring para 1.4/11: no position in the Seller Update is agreed, and silence on any point is not acceptance.

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up schedule or an issues list in the Seller's clause order if that is the preferred format for the next turn.
=== END ADVICE ===
